paragraphs: R' Shimon ben Zoma: Avot, chapter 4; Mishnah Berakhot 1:5; Nazir 8:1; Sotah 9:15; Menahot 11:4; Hullin, chapter 5, mishnah 2 in the cited numbering (5:5 in the compared edition), 83a. He was one of the four who entered the Pardes: he gazed and was stricken. Of him Scripture says, “Have you found honey? Eat what suffices you,” and so forth: Hagigah 14b. This accords with what the sages said in Berakhot 57b: whoever sees Ben Zoma in a dream should expect wisdom, and so forth; therefore his punishment was that wisdom ceased from him and he was stricken. Berit Shalom, Aharei Mot. He was one of the five who argued before the sages; see Danin. A great expositor: Sotah 49a, “When Ben Zoma died, the expositors ceased.” R' Elazar ben Mattyah and Ben Azzai and Hananyah ben Hakhinai. He disagrees with R' Yehoshua. R' Yehoshua greeted him: Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 2. Hesed le-Avraham, spring 5, river 25, writes: Ben Zoma is the mystery of Hevel, for the sparks were intermingled within Hevel, and there is no limb that does not contain six hundred thousand sparks. Ben Zoma had to enter through soul-impregnation and reincarnation with all six hundred thousand, and so forth. This is the secret of what Ben Zoma said when he saw a crowd, “Blessed is He who created all these to serve me”: Berakhot 58a. For whoever is reincarnated with a soul to repair it takes a share in the commandments that it performs. Thus all these six hundred thousand serve him: they perform commandments, and he takes a share with them.
